info.title: HTTP Arena Gateway API
info.description:
Endpoint contract for HTTP Arena **gateway** benchmark profiles. Gateway profiles are orchestrated with Docker Compose and measure the end-to-end throughput of a whole stack on port 8443.

- **gateway-64** (Gateway H2) and **gateway-h3** (Gateway H3) - exactly two services, a production-grade reverse proxy and the framework server, behind HTTP/2 + TLS (or HTTP/3 at the edge for gateway-h3). The proxy serves `/static/*` from disk; the server answers `/baseline2`, `/json/{count}` and `/async-db`. These reuse the endpoints of the [main API spec](/openapi.json) and have no additional contract here. Note that the gateway workload requests `/json/{count}` **without** the `m` multiplier, so a missing `m` must be treated as 1.
- **production-stack** - four services (edge proxy, Redis cache, the shared JWT authsvc, framework server) behind HTTP/2 + TLS. Its endpoints are documented below.

All numeric fields are integers - no floats. JSON responses use lowercase field names.

**Port mapping:**
- `8443` - HTTP/2 + TLS at the edge (ALPN `h2`), and HTTP/3 over QUIC for gateway-h3

See the [main API spec](/openapi.json) for all non-gateway benchmark endpoints.

servers.description: HTTP/2 + TLS at the edge - production-stack profile (ALPN: h2)

tags.name: Production Stack
tags.description:
Full production stack benchmark: four services - edge proxy, Redis cache, the shared JWT authsvc (from `frameworks/_shared/authsvc/`, built as-is) and the framework server - behind HTTPS/H2 on port 8443, at 256 and 1,024 connections.

- `/static/*` is served by the edge from disk (no auth, never reaches the server)
- `/public/*` is forwarded to the server without auth or caching
- `/api/*` is verified by authsvc on **every** request (no auth caching at the edge); the server receives a trusted `X-User-Id` header and never parses JWTs itself

The read workload is 30% `/static/*`, 10% `/public/baseline`, 50% `GET /api/items/{id}` (IDs 1-10,000) and 10% `GET /api/me`, run in parallel with a write workload of `POST /api/items/{id}` for IDs 1-20. All `/api/*` requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`.

**Standard:** Exactly four services. JWT verification must happen at the edge via `auth_request` / `forward_auth` using the shared authsvc - no custom auth. The server must implement cache-aside on `/api/items` reads and invalidation on writes, and must wait on a healthy cache (`depends_on` with `condition: service_healthy`).

**Tuned:** Same four-service shape. May tune proxy configuration, connection pools, CPU split and cache TTLs. May not replace authsvc or skip JWT verification.

**Engine:** No specific rules. May replace any service with a custom implementation.

get.description: Unauthenticated sum endpoint, 10% of the production-stack read workload. Identical behavior to `/baseline11` - returns `a + b` as plain text. The `/public/` prefix separates it from JWT-protected `/api/` endpoints so the edge proxy can route without calling authsvc. Validation sends randomized operands.

Unauthenticated JSON endpoint, no auth and no cache. Identical behavior to `/json/{count}` - returns the first `count` dataset items with computed `total` fields. Validation requests `/public/json/25` without `m`, so a missing `m` must be treated as 1.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Per-request multiplier for `total = price × quantity × m`. Treated as 1 when absent.

get.description:
JWT-authenticated item read, 50% of the read workload (IDs 1-10,000). The edge proxy verifies the `Authorization: Bearer` token via authsvc before forwarding the request; the framework receives a trusted `X-User-Id` header and must **not** perform its own JWT verification.

Implements cache-aside on key `item:{id}`:
1. Check the cache
2. Miss → `SELECT ... FROM items WHERE id = $1`
3. Populate the cache with TTL ≤ 1 second
4. Return the item with `X-Cache: HIT` (served from cache) or `X-Cache: MISS` (fetched from Postgres)

How the cache is built is the framework's choice: two-tier in-process + Redis (e.g. .NET HybridCache), Redis only, in-process only, or the framework's own cache abstraction. Validation reads a cold ID twice and requires `MISS` then `HIT`.

X-Cache.description: `HIT` when served from cache, `MISS` when fetched from Postgres

401.description: Missing or invalid JWT (rejected by authsvc at the edge)

post.summary: Update item and invalidate cache (production-stack profile)
post.description:
JWT-authenticated item update - the write workload, round-robin over IDs 1-20, which are also read so the cache churns. Parses `name`, `price` and `quantity` from the JSON body, runs `UPDATE items SET ... WHERE id = $1` in Postgres, then **invalidates cache key `item:{id}`** in every tier it uses, so the next read is a `MISS`. Returns `204 No Content` on success.

The write path must reject unauthenticated calls just like the read path: validation posts without a token and with a bogus one, and requires `401` both times.

Note: the method is POST (not PUT) because the production-stack workload uses POST for writes - this matches the load generator template.

401.description: Missing or invalid JWT (rejected by authsvc at the edge)

get.description:
JWT-authenticated user profile read, 10% of the read workload. The edge proxy sets `X-User-Id` from the verified JWT `sub` claim; the framework reads this header and performs a cache-aside lookup on `user:{id}` (TTL ≤ 30 seconds) against the `users` table. The benchmark token belongs to user 42.

SQL on cache miss: `SELECT id, name, email, plan FROM users WHERE id = $1`

X-Cache.description: Optional. `HIT` when served from cache, `MISS` when fetched from Postgres

401.description: Missing or invalid JWT (rejected by authsvc at the edge)

BearerAuth.description: HMAC-SHA256 JWT verified by the shared authsvc sidecar on every `/api/*` request, with the secret from its `JWT_SECRET` environment variable. The framework never parses or validates tokens itself - it receives a trusted `X-User-Id` header set by the edge proxy after successful verification. The pre-generated benchmark token (`data/jwt-token.txt`) embeds `{"sub":"42","name":"Alice Chen","exp":<future>}`.

Rating.description: Aggregated item rating. In Postgres it is stored as the `rating_score` and `rating_count` columns and must be restructured into this object.

Item.description: A single item as stored in the Postgres `items` table. Used in async-db and production-stack responses.

ProcessedItem.description: An item from the JSON dataset, unchanged, with a per-request computed `total` field. Used only in `/json/{count}` and `/public/json/{count}` responses.

total.description: Computed per request as `price × quantity × m` - integer arithmetic, no rounding

JsonResponse.description: Response from `GET /json/{count}` and `GET /public/json/{count}`. The `count` field must equal the route parameter and match `items.length`.

count.description: Number of items returned. Must equal the `count` route parameter.

UpdateItemRequest.description: Request body for `POST /api/items/{id}`. Updates `name`, `price`, and `quantity`. The cache entry for the item ID is invalidated on success.

User.description: User profile from the `users` table. Returned by `GET /api/me` after a cache-aside lookup keyed on `user:{id}` (TTL ≤ 30 seconds).
